newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volkswagen denies high error quota reports.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen denies high error quota reports.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG on Monday strongly denied newspaper reports that there were problems with around 30 percent of its car output from its main plant at Wolfsburg.

"The figure of 30 percent is not comparable either internally nor with the competition, as the work processes in each section of the company are different," a spokesman for Volkswagen told Reuters on Monday.
The German Sunday broadsheet Welt am Sonntag said on Sunday that the rate of error at the Wolfsburg plant was well above the industry average at around 30 percent.
The VW spokesman said that productivity had risen 47.3 percent at the Wolfsburg facility between 1993 and 1995.
In absolute terms that means that every employee produced an average of 57 cars a year, up from 38.7 cars annually, the spokesman said.
The Welt am Sonntag report hit sentiment in Volkswagen shares over the day on Monday.
VW ended German bourse trade down 6.30 marks ($4.24) , over one percent, at 543.70 marks, compared to the overall DAX index which was down 10.95 points, or 0.43 percent, at 2,532.88 points.
In afternoon electronic trade, VW shares were down 5.20 marks at 543.50 marks.
